premise.title: The Platform That Arrived Empty
premise.logline: An apprentice station investigator must decide whether a missing night train is a scheduling failure or evidence tampering, when the official manifest and a witness's pocket watch disagree.
premise.immediate_objective: create a bounded evidence record without inventing a culprit
premise.inciting_event: At 02:10 the archive lists train 41 as arriving, but the platform clock never marked its presence.
premise.central_problem: What happened between the signal log and the platform witness statement?
premise.wonder_or_discovery: At 02:10 the archive lists train 41 as arriving, but the platform clock never marked its presence.
premise.stakes: An unearned accusation could destroy a worker's career; a false closure could allow future safety incidents.
constraints: A witness cannot know a sealed dispatch record before its lawful disclosure.
A stopped pocket watch is not proof that the train stopped in time.
A published manifest is not automatically evidence of physical arrival.
No unverified culprit, sabotage mechanism or secret tunnel becomes canon.
premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: The protagonist must choose either seal_provisional_log or reopen_signal_audit before the evidence window closes.
premise.mystery_or_forward_question: What happened between the signal log and the platform witness statement?
premise.local_payoff: Resolve exactly what can be reported from existing observations; leave cause, hidden motives and unverified future outcomes open.
persistent_outcomes_possible: An evidence-bounded report may be recorded only if produced and witnessed in the actual story.
Professional trust may shift only if the story earns that relationship change.
A future follow-up may become eligible but must not be treated as already authorized.
world_specific_elements: mechanical platform clocks, telegraphs, signal logs and manually signed manifests
none; all anomalous events must admit natural evidence-based interpretation
The municipal inquiry must protect innocent employees from unsupported accusations.
Dispatch records require formal release to outsiders.
